An oligarch fabricates evidence. His newspapers blame a foreign country. His government launches a war before anyone can investigate. They steal everything. This playbook is 128 years old today.

February 15, 1898: the USS Maine explodes in Havana Harbor. 

Before any investigation, Hearst's New York Journal prints fabricated blueprints of "secret Spanish torpedoes" that never existed. 

He publishes a $50,000 reward for proof Spain did it. 

He floods the papers with fake atrocity propaganda to vilify Spain.

He refuses to print a single Spanish source. 

The Spanish investigation that concluded it was an internal accident? Blacked out.

The cameraman filming the wreckage arrives... on Hearst's private yacht. The oligarch selling the war produces the visual evidence.

The Maine's own commander Cpt. Sigsbee cables Washington: don't jump to conclusions until we investigate. Hearst's presses drown him out.

Ten weeks later: invasion of Cuba, Puerto Rico, Philippines, Guam.

The following week, Hearst runs a front page headline taking credit: "How do you like the Journal's war?" 

78 years later, the U.S. Navy quietly confirms it was an internal explosion. No Spanish mine. No torpedo. 

Just a fake news pretext and an empire built on it.

Maine. Lusitania. Tonkin. Nayirah. 9/11. 

They never stopped running this play, they just upgraded the cameras.
